You're continuing development of Culprit (team PiedPiper, neatHack 2026). Read HOW_IT_WORKS.md and hackathon.md first; they describe the current state accurately. PROMPTS.md has the answer key.

## Ground rules (important)
- Another session is running paid Culprit runs from /Volumes/DevSSD/Projects/piedpiper-neathacks. Each branch run starts a new process that loads code from that folder. Do NOT edit, check out branches, run uv sync, or touch .culprit/ in that folder.
- Work ONLY in a separate git worktree. Create it first:
    git -C /Volumes/DevSSD/Projects/piedpiper-neathacks worktree add /Volumes/DevSSD/Projects/piedpiper-neathacks-dev -b feat/bench fix/decision-gates
    cp /Volumes/DevSSD/Projects/piedpiper-neathacks/.env /Volumes/DevSSD/Projects/piedpiper-neathacks-dev/
  Then do all work in /Volumes/DevSSD/Projects/piedpiper-neathacks-dev (it gets its own .culprit/ ledger).
- Never modify the RefundDesk repo (/Volumes/DevSSD/Projects/piedpiper-neathacks-refunddesk). Only read it, and only create worktrees from it. Never write the answer key, branch-to-scenario mapping, or words like scenario/regression/culprit/seed into anything in that repo.
- No paid runs (anything that calls a model or the victim on RefundDesk) without asking me first. Build and test on the free fixture (tests/fixtures/make_victim.py).
- Commit only when I say so. Don't push.

## Current state (branch fix/decision-gates, commit 3c75be9)
- Bisect core is built and tested (68 tests): suite pinning, skip, Wilson rule plus resampling, a one-sided Fisher regression gate (alpha 0.05), retries for infrastructure errors (infra_error status), budget caps, resume with SHAs pinned per run, neatlogs tracing plus verify-trace, and Entire intent with the leakage filter.
- Provider: Anthropic (claude-sonnet-5-5) if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set, else OpenRouter z-ai/glm-5.3. This machine has only the OpenRouter key, so GLM is used. Culprit records the victim model per run (Config.victim_provider/victim_model) and passes it to every victim commit.
- First real run: ff50e3620fdd on origin/hist/b with GLM. It found 397c427 (95% Wilson), skipped 22a37db, 240 runs, $0.60, 12.5 min, verify-trace PASS.
- Runs on hist/a, c, d, e, f are in progress in the other session. Results will be logged in hackathon.md.
- RefundDesk clone: /Volumes/DevSSD/Projects/piedpiper-neathacks-refunddesk (only origin/hist/* refs locally, no local hist/* branches). CULPRIT_VICTIM_REPO in .env points at it.
- The entire CLI isn't installed yet, so intent falls back to the commit message and diff.

## Your task: M3, `culprit bench` (PRD §10, §13; PROMPTS.md Prompt G step 1 and Prompt C M3)
1. bench/scenarios.yaml: one entry per branch, with good ref good-v1.0 and bad ref origin/hist/<x>.
2. bench/ground_truth.json: per branch, the culprit SHA, the responsible hunk (file plus line range, from `git show <sha>` in the RefundDesk clone), and the intended-gain metric (latency / tokens / cost). The culprit SHAs, from HOW_IT_WORKS.md §5.2:
   a c4f2401, b 397c427, c acf3b7d, d 441058e, e 8ae122d, f 1777d44 (resolve to full SHAs).
   Uninstallable commits: hist/b 22a37db, hist/f 2ad118e.
3. `culprit bench --scenarios bench/scenarios.yaml --tag v1|v2`: runs each scenario through the existing Orchestrator (sequentially), then scores each against ground truth: culprit correct (or correctly "no_regression" when the bug isn't visible), victim runs used, cost, wall time, and status. It writes evidence/bench-<tag>.md with a table plus run IDs and neatlogs trace IDs. Ground truth must never reach any LLM or Entire text (leakage guard: pass only SHAs).
4. Also support scoring EXISTING runs from the ledger (e.g. `culprit bench --score-runs <run_id>...` or by matching good/bad SHAs), so the runs already made don't need repeating.
5. Tests on the fixture: scoring logic, the yaml/json loaders, and an end-to-end bench on 2 fixture scenarios.
6. Update HOW_IT_WORKS.md (§14, §15) and add a hackathon.md entry. Then tell me what's done and ask before committing.
</pasted_content id="cab8">

1	# How Culprit and RefundDesk work: complete guide
2	
3	> Team PiedPiper · neatHack 2026 · written Sat 10 Oct 2026, ~17:00 IST.
4	> This describes the code **as it exists now**, not the plan. Where the plan (PRD.md) and the code differ, this guide says so. Anything not built yet is marked **NOT BUILT**.
5	
6	---
7	
8	## Contents
9	
10	1. [The idea in one minute](#1-the-idea-in-one-minute)
11	2. [Words used in this guide](#2-words-used-in-this-guide)
12	3. [The two repos and why there are two](#3-the-two-repos-and-why-there-are-two)
13	4. [RefundDesk, the test subject](#4-refunddesk-the-test-subject)
14	5. [The planted bugs (the six branches)](#5-the-planted-bugs-the-six-branches)
15	6. [Culprit, the detective](#6-culprit-the-detective)
16	7. [A complete run, step by step](#7-a-complete-run-step-by-step)
17	8. [The statistics, explained simply](#8-the-statistics-explained-simply)
18	9. [Recovery: what happens when things go wrong](#9-recovery-what-happens-when-things-go-wrong)
19	10. [The ledger (Culprit's memory)](#10-the-ledger-culprits-memory)
20	11. [How the three required tools are used](#11-how-the-three-required-tools-are-used)
21	12. [Keeping the answers secret (leakage guard)](#12-keeping-the-answers-secret-leakage-guard)
22	13. [Money: what things cost](#13-money-what-things-cost)
23	14. [Commands you can run](#14-commands-you-can-run)
24	15. [What is built and what is not](#15-what-is-built-and-what-is-not)
25	16. [Known issues and oddities](#16-known-issues-and-oddities)
26	17. [What happens next](#17-what-happens-next)
27	18. [Appendix A: every RefundDesk test task](#appendix-a-every-refunddesk-test-task)
28	19. [Appendix B: every commit on every branch](#appendix-b-every-commit-on-every-branch)
29	20. [Appendix C: file-by-file map](#appendix-c-file-by-file-map)
30	21. [Appendix D: environment variables and runtime paths](#appendix-d-environment-variables-and-runtime-paths)
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 1. The idea in one minute
35	
36	Teams that build AI agents keep changing them: prompts, models, tools, retry settings. Often a coding agent writes the change. Sometimes the agent quietly gets worse. Finding *which* change broke it is painful, for two reasons:
37	
38	- You have to re-run the tests at many old versions.
39	- AI agents are **random**: the same version can pass a test one time and fail it the next. A single run per version can't be trusted.
40	
41	**Culprit** does that search automatically. You give it:
42	
43	- a version you know was **good** (here, git tag `good-v1.0`)
44	- a version you know is **bad** (for example, branch `hist/b`)
45	- a set of **test tasks** (the "eval suite")
46	
47	Culprit then:
48	
49	1. **Confirms something really broke.** It runs every test task several times on both versions and checks the difference isn't just luck.
50	2. **Searches the history by halving it**, like `git bisect`: test the middle commit, keep the half that contains the break, repeat. 14 commits need about 4 tests instead of 14.
51	3. **Copes with randomness.** It runs each test several times, uses a statistics rule to decide "good", "bad" or "not sure yet", and runs more tests when it isn't sure.
52	4. **Copes with broken commits.** If a commit won't even install, it skips it and tests a neighbour.
53	5. **Names the guilty commit**, then asks **Entire** *why* that change was made, using the recorded coding-agent session behind the commit.
54	6. **Records everything**: every test run, cost and decision goes into a database, and every step is traced in **neatlogs**.
55	
56	Planned but **NOT BUILT** yet:
57	
58	- pointing at the exact guilty lines inside the commit
59	- writing a minimal fix and proving it works
60	- generating a report
61	- scoring itself on a benchmark
62	
63	To show it working, we built a realistic victim, **RefundDesk**, and planted six bugs in its history. In each case we know the right answer, so we can check Culprit honestly.
64	
65	---
66	
67	## 2. Words used in this guide
68	
69	| Word | Meaning here |
70	|---|---|
71	| **Agent** | A program where an AI model decides which tools to call, e.g. "look up order", "issue refund". |
72	| **Victim** | The agent being investigated, here RefundDesk. |
73	| **Eval / task / test task** | One scripted customer situation plus an automatic pass/fail check. Example: "customer wants a refund for an $89 order; the refund tool fails once; the refund must still happen exactly once." |
74	| **Eval suite** | All the tasks together: 26 main tasks and 6 "held-out" tasks. |
75	| **Repetition (k)** | How many times each task runs on a commit. Default 3. Each repetition uses a different seed (0, 1, 2). |
76	| **Seed** | A number that makes the fake tool failures repeatable. The same task with the same seed always gets the same injected failures. |
77	| **Pass rate** | Passes divided by runs, e.g. 28/30. |
78	| **Bisect** | Finding the first bad commit by repeatedly testing the middle of the remaining range. |
79	| **Commit / SHA** | One saved change in git; the SHA is its ID (e.g. `397c427`). |
80	| **Branch** | A named line of commits. Our six test histories are `hist/a` … `hist/f`. |
81	| **Tag** | A permanent label on one commit. `good-v1.0` marks the known-good version. |
82	| **Worktree** | An extra checkout of the same git repo in a separate folder. Culprit uses one per commit, so it never touches your real folder. |
83	| **Wilson interval / CI** | A range like `[0.70, 0.99]`: "we're 95% sure the true pass rate is somewhere in here". See [§8](#8-the-statistics-explained-simply). |
84	| **Threshold (t)** | The halfway line between the good and bad pass rates. Above it means "good", below it means "bad". |
85	| **GOOD / BAD / INCONCLUSIVE / SKIP** | Culprit's verdict on a commit. SKIP means "couldn't even install it". |
86	| **Ledger** | Culprit's SQLite database of everything it did (`.culprit/ledger.sqlite`). |
87	| **Trace / span** | neatlogs' record of a run: a tree of steps (spans), each with inputs, outputs, timing and errors. |
88	| **Checkpoint** | Entire's record linking a git commit to the coding-agent session that produced it, including what was asked and why. |
89	| **Intent** | The "why" behind a commit, taken from its Entire checkpoint. |
90	| **Planted bug / regression** | A change we deliberately made to RefundDesk that makes it worse. |
91	| **Fixture** | A tiny fake victim repo that Culprit's tests generate. It has no AI calls, so it's free. |
92	
93	---
94	
95	## 3. The two repos and why there are two
96	
97	```
98	neathack/
99	├── piedpiper-neathacks/   ← Culprit (the product)  → github.com/rahilmavani/piedpiper-neathacks (public)
100	└── refunddesk/            ← RefundDesk (the victim) → github.com/rahilmavani/piedpiper-neathacks-refunddesk (private)
101	```
102	
103	**Why separate?**
104	
105	1. **Clean history.** Culprit bisects RefundDesk's commits. If Culprit's own code lived in the same history, every bisect step would wade through unrelated commits.
106	2. **Entire records each repo separately.** Culprit reads Entire sessions from the victim repo to find intent. Our planning sessions (which mention the answers) happen in the Culprit repo, so they can never leak into the victim's records.
107	3. **Parallel work.** One coding session can switch branches in RefundDesk while another builds Culprit, without stepping on each other.
108	4. **Realism.** A customer would point Culprit at *their* agent repo: `culprit run --repo ../refunddesk …`.
109	
110	**How they connect at run time.** Culprit never edits the RefundDesk folder. For each commit it wants to test, it:
111	
112	- creates a worktree under `piedpiper-neathacks/.culprit/worktrees/<sha>`
113	- installs it with `uv sync --locked`
114	- runs RefundDesk's own test runner there as a subprocess: `python -m refunddesk.eval --task <id> --seed <n>`
115	- reads the one line of JSON it prints, which includes passed, cost, latency, tokens and trace ID
116	
117	Both repos have:
118	- Entire enabled (`.entire/settings.json`, checkpoints stored as git refs)
119	- Claude Code hooks that let Entire record sessions (`.claude/settings.json`)
120	- co-author lines turned off (`includeCoAuthoredBy: false`, empty `attribution`)
121	- a gitignored `.env` holding `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic`, `VICTIM_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5` and, in the Culprit repo, `REDACTED`
122	
123	---
124	
125	## 4. RefundDesk, the test subject
126	
127	### 4.1 What it is
128	
129	RefundDesk is a customer-support agent for an online store. A customer writes something like "Order A1009, wrong size shoes, I want my money back". The agent uses tools to look up the order, apply the refund policy, refund or escalate to a human, and email the customer.
130	
131	- Python 3.12, managed with `uv`. Package `refunddesk` v0.1.0.
132	- Model: **Claude Sonnet 5.5** (`claude-sonnet-5-5`) via the Anthropic API when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, otherwise **GLM 5.3** (`z-ai/glm-5.3`) via OpenRouter. All baseline numbers below were measured on Sonnet 5.5; a GLM run needs its own baseline.
133	- Temperature 0 is requested. Sonnet 5.5 rejects the temperature setting, so the client detects that and stops sending it (cached in `.cache/refunddesk/sampling.json`).
134	- The tools are **mocks**: they read and write a JSON file, not a real store. That makes every test fast, free of side effects and repeatable.
135	
136	### 4.2 The rules the agent follows (system prompt, on `main` and `good-v1.0`)
137	
138	```
139	1. Always look up the order with lookup_order before acting on it.
140	2. Never issue a refund when the order lookup failed (status failed, error, or timed out).
141	   In that case do not refund; escalate to a human with escalate_to_human and tell the customer.
142	3. If the order is not found, do not refund; escalate to a human (order_id "unknown" is allowed).
143	4. Refunds over $500 must be escalated to a human. Never call issue_refund for more than $500.
144	   A refund of exactly $500.00 or less may be issued by you.
145	5. At most one refund per order; never refund an already-"refunded" order; refund the full
146	   amount unless the customer asks for a specific smaller amount.
147	6. After a refund or escalation, send the customer one short email (to the address they asked
148	   for, otherwise the order's customer_email).
149	7. No refund/escalation when the customer only asks a question; use get_refund_policy for policy.
150	8. Remember details the customer gave earlier in the conversation.
151	9. Act within policy without asking for confirmation unless information is missing.
152	Reply to the customer in two or three short sentences.
153	```
154	
155	### 4.3 How one conversation turn runs (`src/refunddesk/agent.py`)
156	
157	1. The customer message is added to the conversation history.
158	2. The agent calls the model with the system prompt, the recent history and the tool definitions. This repeats up to **12 steps per turn**.
159	3. If the model replies with plain text and no tool calls, the turn ends and that text goes to the customer.
160	4. If the model asks for tools, each tool call goes through:
161	   1. **Strict argument check** (`parse_tool_arguments`). Unknown tool, broken JSON, duplicate keys, missing or extra fields, wrong types, NaN or booleans-as-numbers are all rejected with an error result.
162	   2. **Policy guard in code** (`_policy_block`, refunds only). The refund is blocked if the order wasn't successfully looked up first, or if the lookup failed, or if the amount is over $500. This guard is code, not prompt, so the model can't talk its way past it.
163	   3. **Run with retries** (`_execute_with_retries`). Up to **4 attempts** (`MAX_RETRIES = 3`):
164	      - a timeout is retried
165	      - a result that fails validation is retried; see the next step
166	      - if all attempts fail, the model gets `{"status":"error", "error":"… failed after 3 retries …"}`
167	   4. **Result validation** (`validate_tool_result`). A result with `status: "failed"`, a malformed result, or a lookup missing order fields counts as invalid and gets retried. **This is the safety net that the hero bug removes.**
168	   5. A successful lookup is remembered (`verified_orders`); a failed lookup is remembered too (`failed_lookups`).
169	5. All tool results go back to the model, and the loop continues.
170	6. After 12 steps with no final answer, the agent gives up politely: "A human agent will follow up."
171	
172	**History window.** Only the last 24 messages are sent to the model. The cut always starts at a customer message, so a tool call is never separated from its result. Configurable via `REFUNDDESK_HISTORY_WINDOW`.
173	
174	### 4.4 The mock tools (`src/refunddesk/tools.py`)
175	
176	| Tool | Inputs | What it does |
177	|---|---|---|
178	| `lookup_order` | `order_id` | Returns the order, or `not_found` |
179	| `get_refund_policy` | none | Returns the policy: $500 agent limit, 30-day window, partial refunds allowed, no duplicates |
180	| `issue_refund` | `order_id`, `amount`, `reason` | Rejects unknown orders and amounts ≤ 0 or above what's left to refund; otherwise records refund `RF-nnnn` and marks the order refunded when fully refunded |
181	| `escalate_to_human` | `order_id`, `reason` | Records ticket `ESC-nnnn` (`order_id "unknown"` allowed) |
182	| `send_customer_email` | `to`, `subject`, `body` | Records email `MSG-nnnn` |
183	
184	Every tool call is written to a **call log** (`seq`, tool, args, outcome, result), which the checkers inspect afterwards. Outcomes are `ok`, `not_found`, `rejected`, `timeout`, `failed`, `blocked` and `invalid_arguments`.
185	
186	### 4.5 Fake failures, on purpose (`src/refunddesk/faults.py`)
187	
188	To test whether the agent is robust, tasks can make tools misbehave:
189	
190	- **`timeout`**: the tool raises a timeout. In neatlogs the span is marked ERROR.
191	- **`failed`**: the tool returns `{"status":"failed","error":"<tool>: upstream service error"}`.
192	
193	A fault rule says which tool fails and when:
194	
195	- `calls: [1,2]` means the 1st and 2nd attempts
196	- `always: true`
197	- `rate: 0.5` means randomly, but repeatably, decided by a hash of (task, seed, tool, call number)
198	- `max: N` means at most N times
199	
200	Attempts include retries. So `calls: [1,2,3]` with 3 retries means the **4th attempt succeeds**. The fault fires *before* the tool touches the store, so a failed call has no side effects.
201	
202	### 4.6 The test tasks and checkers
203	
204	Each task is a JSON file in `evals/` containing:
205	- an `id`
206	- the customer message(s) (`turns`)
207	- the starting store (orders)
208	- optional `faults`
209	- `checks`, the pass/fail rules
210	
211	The checkers (`src/refunddesk/checks.py`) are plain code; no AI judges anything:
212	
213	| Checker | Passes when |
214	|---|---|
215	| `refund_count(order_id, count)` | exactly *count* refunds for that order |
216	| `refund_amount(order_id, amount)` | refunds add up to that amount (±0.005) |
217	| `no_refund([order_id])` | no refund (for that order, or at all) |
218	| `escalated([order_id])` | at least one escalation |
219	| `not_escalated` | no escalations |
220	| `email_sent([to])` | at least one email (to that address) |
221	| `tool_called(tool, min, max)` | the tool was attempted between min and max times (failed and timed-out attempts count) |
222	| `refunds_follow_successful_lookup` | every refund came after a successful lookup of the same order |
223	| `injected_fault_seen(tool, kind)` | the planned fault really happened |
224	| `no_refund_over`, `tool_not_called` | exist, but no task uses them |
225	
226	A task **passes** only if the run had no crash and every check passed.
227	
228	There are **26 main tasks and 6 held-out tasks**; all are listed in [Appendix A](#appendix-a-every-refunddesk-test-task).
229	- **20 main tasks** existed at `good-v1.0`.
230	- **6 harder tasks** were added on `main` later (commit `ba86ed0`), after we found the hero bug was too subtle. In these, a tool fails 2–3 times in a row and must be retried. They check the exact number of attempts (e.g. `issue_refund` attempted exactly 4 times), which only the original retry-plus-validation code produces.
231	
232	### 4.7 Running a task (`python -m refunddesk.eval`)
233	
234	```
235	uv run python -m refunddesk.eval --task refund_small_order --seed 1 [--tool-log]
236	```
237	
238	This creates a temporary store, runs the conversation, runs the checks, and prints **one line of JSON** with:
239	- `passed`, `cost` (USD), `latency` (s), `tokens`
240	- `trace_id` (neatlogs)
241	- `llm_calls`, `tool_executions`, `tool_outcomes`
242	- `checks`, `error`, `metadata`
243	
244	It exits 0 even when the task fails; exit 2 means it couldn't start.
245	
246	`python -m refunddesk.suite --reps 3` runs the whole suite in parallel (4 workers), saves results under `.cache/refunddesk/runs/`, and prints pass counts and total cost.
247	
248	### 4.8 RefundDesk's neatlogs tracing (`src/refunddesk/tracing.py`)
249	
250	Every task run is **one trace** in neatlogs, workflow `refunddesk-eval`:
251	
252	```
253	WORKFLOW refunddesk.run_task            ← tagged with culprit_run_id, commit_sha, task_id, repetition, seed
254	└─ AGENT refunddesk.handle_turn         ← one per customer turn
255	   ├─ LLM anthropic.messages.create     ← every model call (captured by neatlogs.wrap)
256	   └─ TOOL <tool name>                  ← every tool attempt; timeouts show as ERROR
257	```
258	
259	When Culprit runs a task, it passes `CULPRIT_RUN_ID`, `COMMIT_SHA`, `TASK_ID` and `REPETITION` as environment variables, so every RefundDesk trace can be matched to the Culprit run, commit and repetition that caused it.
260	
261	`scripts/neatlogs_readback.py` reads traces back through the neatlogs CLI and checks that they're complete: one root, correct parents, span counts that match, metadata present, model and token data present. **All 78 baseline traces passed** that check.
262	
263	### 4.9 Baseline numbers (measured)
264	
265	| What | Result |
266	|---|---|
267	| Full suite (20+6 tasks) × 3 repetitions at the baseline code | **78/78 passed** |
268	| Cost of those 78 runs | **$1.27** (about $0.016 per run) |
269	| Average run time | 6.9 s, almost all of it waiting for the model |
270	| Cheapest / most expensive task | ~$0.007 (status question) / ~$0.028 (multi-turn) |
271	| Unit tests (no AI calls) | 27 pass |
272	| Readback check of all 78 traces | 78/78 pass |
273	
274	---
275	
276	## 5. The planted bugs (the six branches)
277	
278	### 5.1 How the history was built
279	
280	- **`good-v1.0`** points at commit `0479c27` on `main`. The agent code there is identical to `a89cc91`, where the 78/78 baseline was measured.
281	- From `good-v1.0`, six branches `hist/a` … `hist/f` were created. Each one has:

381	## 7. A complete run, step by step
382	
383	Command:
384	```
385	uv run culprit run --repo ../refunddesk --good good-v1.0 --bad hist/b
386	```
387	
388	### 7.1 Set up
389	- Create a run in the ledger (`run_id` = 12 random hex characters, status `running`).
390	- Open the neatlogs root span `culprit_run` and record its trace ID.
391	- List the candidate commits: `git rev-list --first-parent --reverse good..bad`. Oldest first; excludes good, includes bad. For `hist/b` that's 14 commits.
392	
393	### 7.2 Pin the test suite
394	- Take one snapshot of `evals/` from the victim's `main` (via `git archive`) into `.culprit/suites/…`.
395	- Record its source and commit SHA in the ledger.
396	- Before each commit is tested, that snapshot **replaces** the commit's own `evals/`. So every commit faces the same 26 tasks.
397	- A resumed run reuses the recorded snapshot, even if `main` has moved on since.
398	- Alternatively, `--suite /some/folder` uses a folder; its contents are fingerprinted, and a changed folder makes resume refuse.
399	
400	### 7.3 Find the tasks
401	- Read the task names from the snapshot (top level only, so `heldout/` is excluded) and save them in the run's config.
402	
403	### 7.4 Measure both ends (the baseline)
404	- Run **every task × k** on the good commit and on the bad commit. With 26 tasks and k=3, that's 78 runs each, 156 total. **This is the most expensive part of a run.**
405	- If either end fails to install, stop: "cannot bisect".
406	- Compute each end's pass rate and 95% range.
407	- **Safety gate:** a one-sided Fisher exact test asks whether good really passes more often than bad. If p ≥ 0.05 (`gate_alpha`), stop with status **`no_regression`**: Culprit refuses to hunt for a bug that might just be noise.
408	  - This replaced an "intervals overlap" rule, which was much stricter than a 5% test. Under it, 57/60 vs 48/60 (about 3 broken tasks out of 20) was called noise. On a perfect 78/78 baseline, the Fisher gate bisects once about 5 runs fail, while 1–2 flaky failures still count as noise.
409	
410	### 7.5 Choose the "telling" tasks
411	- Rank tasks by how much worse they did on the bad version (good rate minus bad rate).
412	- Keep the top **8** that actually dropped. These are the tasks most likely to reveal the bug, so each bisect step runs only these.
413	- This is plain code today; the planned AI-assisted selection is **NOT BUILT**.
414	
415	### 7.6 Bisect
416	- Start with "the last good commit is before #1, the first bad commit is #14".
417	- Repeatedly test the middle of that range:
418	  1. Make a worktree for the commit, copy in the pinned suite, run `uv sync --locked`.
419	     - **If the install fails, the commit is SKIP**, and the next candidate is tested: middle+1, then middle−1, then +2, −2 and so on.
420	  2. Run the 8 telling tasks × 3 repetitions (24 runs), in parallel with 4 workers.
421	  3. Decide GOOD, BAD or INCONCLUSIVE ([§8](#8-the-statistics-explained-simply)).
422	  4. If INCONCLUSIVE, resample:
423	     - **Round 1:** 3 more repetitions of the same 8 tasks.
424	     - **Round 2:** up to 8 *other* tasks × 3, but only tasks that also dropped from good to bad. If there are none, 3 more repetitions of the same 8 instead. A task that passes on both ends tells good from bad apart no better than a coin, and it pulls the threshold up.
425	     - Still unsure: decide by the plain pass rate and mark the step **`low_confidence`**.
426	     - At most 72 runs per commit.
427	  5. GOOD moves the "last good" marker up; BAD moves the "first bad" marker down.
428	- Stop when the two markers are adjacent. The first bad commit is the culprit.
429	- If skipped commits sit exactly on the boundary, the result is a **range** of suspects (status `ambiguous`), the same way `git bisect skip` reports it.
430	
431	### 7.7 Ask Entire why
432	- Run `entire checkpoint explain <sha>` in the victim repo and take the **Intent** section.
433	- If the Intent is empty or is a system message, read the session's typed prompts from `--transcript`.
434	- If the commit has no checkpoint, fall back to the commit message plus the diff, and say "intent unavailable".
435	- Pass the text through the **leakage filter** ([§12](#12-keeping-the-answers-secret-leakage-guard)) and store it with the diff in the ledger.
436	
437	### 7.8 Finish
438	- Print and store the result. Example from the free demo:
439	  `Culprit: a419a7d… 'speed up tool handling' (confidence: 95% Wilson)`
440	- Possible statuses: `found`, `no_regression`, `ambiguous`, `budget_exceeded`, `infra_error`, `error`.
441	- Output is the terminal log plus the ledger. A report file is **NOT BUILT**.
442

462	## 8. The statistics, explained simply
463	
464	**The problem.** If a commit passes 13 of 15 runs, is it good? Probably, but with only 15 runs, luck matters.
465	
466	**Wilson interval.** From passes and runs, Culprit computes a range where the true pass rate almost certainly lies (95% sure):
467	- 14/15 gives `[0.70, 0.99]`: the true rate is somewhere between 70% and 99%.
468	- 1/15 gives `[0.01, 0.30]`.
469	- More runs make the range narrower.
470	
471	The formula (`stats.wilson`), with p = passes/n and z = 1.96:
472	```
473	centre = (p + z²/2n) / (1 + z²/n)
474	half   = z·√(p(1−p)/n + z²/4n²) / (1 + z²/n)
475	range  = [centre − half, centre + half], clipped to [0, 1]
476	```
477	
478	**Threshold.** The halfway point between the good and bad pass rates, calculated for the **same tasks** the commit ran. This matters because some tasks fail more on the bad version than others.
479	
480	**Decision (`stats.decide`):**
481	- whole range at or above the threshold → **GOOD**
482	- whole range at or below the threshold → **BAD**
483	- range straddles the threshold → **INCONCLUSIVE**, so run more tests
484	
485	**Why it matters.** A naive bisect that runs each test once would sometimes blame the wrong commit because of one unlucky failure. Culprit only commits to a verdict when the evidence is strong, and it labels any verdict it had to guess (`low_confidence`).
486

489	## 9. Recovery: what happens when things go wrong
490	
491	| Problem | How Culprit notices | What it does |
492	|---|---|---|
493	| Victim run hit an API problem (429, 5xx, overloaded, connection), timed out, or printed no JSON | Error text from the victim runner | Retries it twice with backoff (5 s, 20 s). It is never recorded as a failed task. If it keeps failing, the run stops with `infra_error`, and `culprit resume` continues |
494	| Bad key, missing config or unknown model | `AuthenticationError`, `ConfigError`, … | Stops at once with `infra_error`, without recording anything against the commit |
495	| Commit won't install | `uv sync --locked` fails | Marks it SKIP and tests a neighbour |
496	| Unsure result (e.g. 3/5) | Range straddles the threshold | Runs more repetitions, then more tasks, then decides by point estimate and flags `low_confidence` |
497	| Process killed mid-run | The ledger has partial work | `culprit resume <run_id>` redoes only the missing task runs; no duplicates (tested by kill −9 and resume) |
498	| Budget reached | Cost total ≥ cap, checked before each batch | Stops, reports the best current suspect range, tells you how to resume with a higher cap |
499	| Good and bad not really different | Ranges overlap | Stops with `no_regression` |
500	| Victim crashes because of the commit's own code (e.g. `KeyError`) | Error text is not an infrastructure error | Counts as a failed task: that's the commit's behaviour |
501	| No Entire checkpoint | `explain` finds no checkpoint | Uses commit message + diff; says "intent unavailable" |
502	| Entire Intent is a system tag | Intent starts with `<` or `*(` | Reads the session's typed prompts from `--transcript` |
503	
504	Also: `culprit resume` re-uses the good and bad SHAs recorded at the start of the run, so moving a branch mid-run can't change the range. An empty range (good = bad) stops before the expensive baselines.

582	## 12. Keeping the answers secret (leakage guard)
583	
584	We know which commit is guilty on each branch. If Culprit's AI parts could see that, the benchmark would be meaningless. The protections:
585	
586	1. **Neutral names in the victim repo:** `hist/a`…`hist/f`. No commit or comment mentions scenarios, gaps or regressions (scanned; clean).
587	2. **The answer key lives only in the Culprit repo** (`PROMPTS.md`, this file, and later `bench/`). Culprit never feeds its own repo's files to an AI.
588	3. **Only the examined commit's checkpoint is read**, never its neighbours'.
589	4. **Leakage filter** (`entire.leak_filter`): before any Entire text is stored or used, it drops every line containing any of:
590	   - `R1`–`R6` as whole words
591	   - `hist/`, `scenario`, `culprit`, `regression`, `seed`, `gap` or `pause` (any case, even inside longer words)
592	   - the name of any branch or tag in the victim repo except main, master, origin and HEAD
593	
594	   The number of removed lines is logged.
595	5. **One accident, cleaned up:** an early RefundDesk session read `PROMPTS.md`. It stopped before building anything, and its Entire record was deleted before it made any commit.
596	
597	The filter is deliberately broad. It also drops harmless lines containing words like "seeded".

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path

import typer
from dotenv import load_dotenv

from culprit import providers, tracing
from culprit.config import DEFAULT_DB, PROJECT_ROOT, Config
from culprit.ledger import Ledger
from culprit.orchestrator import Orchestrator

app = typer.Typer(add_completion=False, help="git bisect for agent behaviour, with receipts.")


@app.command()
def run(
    good: str = typer.Option(..., help="Known-good ref"),
    bad: str = typer.Option(..., help="Known-bad ref"),
    repo: Path = typer.Option(PROJECT_ROOT.parent / "refunddesk", envvar="CULPRIT_VICTIM_REPO",
                              help="Victim repo (only worktrees are created)"),
    suite: str = typer.Option("evals", help="Suite directory in the victim (taken at --suite-ref), "
                              "or a directory on disk (absolute or containing '/')"),
    suite_ref: str = typer.Option("main", help="Victim ref whose suite judges every commit"),
    k: int = typer.Option(3, help="Repetitions per task"),
    budget_usd: float = typer.Option(3.00, help="Hard cost cap for this run"),
    db: Path = typer.Option(DEFAULT_DB, help="Ledger path"),
    workers: int = typer.Option(4, help="Parallel victim task runs"),
) -> None:
    """Find the commit between GOOD and BAD that broke the agent."""
    try:
        victim = providers.select("VICTIM_MODEL")
    except providers.ProviderError as exc:
        typer.echo(f"error: {exc}", err=True)
        raise typer.Exit(2) from exc
    cfg = Config(repo=str(repo.resolve()), good_ref=good, bad_ref=bad, suite=suite, suite_ref=suite_ref, k=k,
                 budget_usd=budget_usd, victim_provider=victim.name, victim_model=victim.model)
    orch = Orchestrator(Ledger(db), cfg, log=typer.echo, workers=workers)
    run_id = orch.start()
    typer.echo(f"run_id {run_id}")
    outcome = orch.run(run_id)
    typer.echo(f"neatlogs session: {run_id}" if tracing.enabled() else "neatlogs tracing off (no NEATLOGS_API_KEY)")
    raise typer.Exit(0 if outcome.status in {"found", "no_regression"} else 1)


@app.command()
def resume(
    run_id: str,
    db: Path = typer.Option(DEFAULT_DB, help="Ledger path"),
    workers: int = typer.Option(4, help="Parallel victim task runs"),
    budget_usd: float | None = typer.Option(None, help="Raise the per-run cost cap (e.g. after budget_exceeded)"),
) -> None:
    """Continue a run without re-executing completed steps."""
    ledger = Ledger(db)
    row = ledger.get_run(run_id)
    cfg = Config.from_json(row["config_json"])
    if budget_usd is not None:
        cfg = replace(cfg, budget_usd=budget_usd)
        ledger.update_config(run_id, row["suite_hash"], cfg.to_json())
    outcome = Orchestrator(ledger, cfg, log=typer.echo, workers=workers).run(run_id)
    raise typer.Exit(0 if outcome.status in {"found", "no_regression"} else 1)


@app.command("verify-trace")
def verify_trace(
    run_id: str,
    db: Path = typer.Option(DEFAULT_DB, help="Ledger path"),
) -> None:
    """Read a run's Culprit traces back from neatlogs and audit them against the trace contract."""
    from culprit.readback import audit

    traces = (Ledger(db).get_artifact(run_id, "neatlogs_traces") or "").split()
    if not traces:
        typer.echo(f"no neatlogs trace recorded for run {run_id}")
        raise typer.Exit(1)
    failed = False
    for trace_id in traces:
        result = audit(trace_id, run_id)
        typer.echo(f"trace {trace_id}: finalized={result.finalized} workflow={result.workflow} "
                   f"session={result.session} spans={result.span_count}")
        typer.echo("  " + ", ".join(f"{k}×{v}" for k, v in sorted(result.by_name.items())))
        for problem in result.problems:
            typer.echo(f"  PROBLEM {problem}")
        typer.echo("  PASS" if result.ok else "  FAIL")
        failed |= not result.ok
    raise typer.Exit(1 if failed else 0)


def main() -> None:
    load_dotenv(PROJECT_ROOT / ".env")
    tracing.init()
    try:
        app()
    finally:
        tracing.shutdown()

from culprit.ledger import Ledger, TaskRun
from culprit.providers import Provider, ProviderError
from culprit.stats import Decision, decide, fisher_one_sided, wilson

Log = Callable[[str], None]


class BudgetExceeded(RuntimeError):
    pass


class InfraError(RuntimeError):
    """A victim run failed for infrastructure reasons (API, config, timeout), not because of the commit."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StepResult:
    sha: str
    skipped: bool
    runs: list[TaskRun]

    @property
    def n(self) -> int:
        return len(self.runs)

    @property
    def passes(self) -> int:
        return sum(r.passed for r in self.runs)

    @property
    def rate(self) -> float:
        return self.passes / self.n if self.n else 0.0

    def task_rates(self) -> dict[str, float]:
        by_task: dict[str, list[bool]] = {}
        for r in self.runs:
            by_task.setdefault(r.task_id, []).append(r.passed)
        return {t: sum(v) / len(v) for t, v in by_task.items()}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Outcome:
    run_id: str
    status: str
    result: BisectResult | None
    summary: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Baselines:
    good: StepResult
    bad: StepResult

    def threshold(self, runs: list[TaskRun]) -> float:
        """Midpoint of the good and bad pass rates over the same task mix as `runs` (PRD §8.1 step 2)."""
        g, b = self.good.task_rates(), self.bad.task_rates()
        return sum((g[r.task_id] + b[r.task_id]) / 2 for r in runs) / len(runs)

    def drop(self, task_id: str) -> float:
        """How much a task's pass rate fell from good to bad."""
        return self.good.task_rates()[task_id] - self.bad.task_rates().get(task_id, 0.0)


def suite_hash(tasks: list[str]) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256("\n".join(tasks).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]


class Orchestrator:
    def __init__(self, ledger: Ledger, cfg: Config, log: Log = print, workers: int = 4):
        self.ledger = ledger
        self.cfg = cfg
        self.repo = Path(cfg.repo).resolve()
        self.log = log
        self.workers = workers
        self.victim = Provider(cfg.victim_provider, cfg.victim_model) if cfg.victim_provider else None
        self.env = victim_env(self.repo, self.victim)
        self.pinned: suite.PinnedSuite | None = None

    # one commit ---------------------------------------------------------------
    def evaluate(self, run_id: str, kind: str, sha: str, tasks: list[str], reps: range) -> StepResult:
        with tracing.span(f"evaluate_commit:{kind}", "CHAIN", commit_sha=sha,
                          input={"kind": kind, "tasks": tasks, "repetitions": [reps.start, reps.stop]}) as sp:
            result = self._evaluate(run_id, kind, sha, tasks, reps)
            sp.output({"skipped": result.skipped, "passes": result.passes, "n": result.n})
            return result

    def _evaluate(self, run_id: str, kind: str, sha: str, tasks: list[str], reps: range) -> StepResult:
        existing = self.ledger.get_step(run_id, kind, sha)
        if existing is not None and existing["status"] == "skip":
            return StepResult(sha, True, [])
        step_id = self.ledger.open_step(run_id, kind, sha)
        done = self.ledger.task_runs(step_id)
        todo = [(t, r) for t in tasks for r in reps if (t, r) not in done]
        if todo:
            worktree = self._worktree(sha)
            assert self.pinned is not None, "suite must be pinned before evaluating"
            suite.install_into(self.pinned, worktree, self.cfg.suite_target)
            with tracing.span("uv_sync_locked", "TOOL", input={"worktree": worktree.name}) as sp:
                installed = sandbox.install(worktree, self.cfg.eval_module, self.cfg.install_timeout_s)
                sp.output({"ok": installed.ok, "log_tail": installed.log[-1500:]})
            if not installed.ok:
                self.ledger.close_step(step_id, "skip", decision=Verdict.SKIP, error=installed.log[-2000:])
                self.log(f"  {sha[:10]} install failed → SKIP")
                return StepResult(sha, True, [])
            self._run_tasks(run_id, step_id, worktree, sha, todo)
        runs = [r for r in self.ledger.task_runs(step_id).values() if r.task_id in tasks and r.repetition in reps]
        result = StepResult(sha, False, runs)
        low, high = wilson(result.passes, result.n, self.cfg.z)
        latencies = [r.latency_ms for r in runs if r.latency_ms is not None]
        self.ledger.close_step(
            step_id, "done", decision=existing["decision"] if existing is not None else None,
            wilson_low=low, wilson_high=high, n=result.n, passes=result.passes,
            cost_usd=sum(r.cost_usd or 0.0 for r in runs),
            latency_ms_p50=statistics.median(latencies) if latencies else None,
        )
        return result

    def _worktree(self, sha: str) -> Path:
        with tracing.span("git_worktree_add", "TOOL", input={"sha": sha}) as sp:
            path = sandbox.add_worktree(self.repo, sha)
            sp.output({"worktree": path.name})
            return path

    def _check_budget(self, run_id: str) -> None:
        if self.ledger.run_cost(run_id) >= self.cfg.budget_usd:
            raise BudgetExceeded(f"run cost reached the ${self.cfg.budget_usd:.2f} per-run cap")
        if self.ledger.total_cost() >= self.cfg.global_budget_usd:
            raise BudgetExceeded(f"ledger total reached the ${self.cfg.global_budget_usd:.2f} global cap")

    def _run_tasks(self, run_id: str, step_id: int, worktree: Path, sha: str, todo: list[tuple[str, int]]) -> None:
        """Workers only run subprocesses; ledger writes and budget checks stay on this thread."""

        def attempt(item: tuple[str, int], n: int) -> TaskRun:
            with tracing.span("victim_eval_run", "TOOL", input={"task_id": item[0], "repetition": item[1],
                                                               "attempt": n}) as sp:
                tr = run_task(worktree, self.env, self.cfg.eval_module, item[0], item[1], run_id=run_id,
                              commit_sha=sha, timeout_s=self.cfg.task_timeout_s)
                sp.output({"passed": tr.passed, "cost_usd": tr.cost_usd, "latency_ms": tr.latency_ms,
                           "victim_trace_id": tr.trace_id, "error": tr.error, "infra": infra_failure(tr)})
                return tr

        def one(item: tuple[str, int]) -> TaskRun:
            """Retry transient infrastructure failures; they are never recorded as failed tasks."""
            for n in range(self.cfg.infra_retries + 1):
                tr = attempt(item, n)
                kind = infra_failure(tr)
                if kind is None:
                    return tr
                if kind == "fatal":
                    raise InfraError(f"{item[0]} rep {item[1]}: {tr.error}")
                if n < self.cfg.infra_retries:
                    time.sleep(self.cfg.infra_backoff_s * 4**n)
            raise InfraError(f"{item[0]} rep {item[1]} still failing after {self.cfg.infra_retries} retries: "
                             f"{tr.error}")

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=self.workers) as pool:
            for start in range(0, len(todo), self.workers):
                self._check_budget(run_id)
                batch = todo[start : start + self.workers]
                # Copy the context per task so each span parents under the current step.
                futures = [pool.submit(contextvars.copy_context().run, one, item) for item in batch]
                errors: list[InfraError] = []
                for fut in futures:  # record every finished run before surfacing an error
                    try:
                        self.ledger.record_task_run(step_id, fut.result())
                    except InfraError as exc:
                        errors.append(exc)
                if errors:
                    raise errors[0]

    # noise-aware classification (PRD §8.1 step 4, §8.2) ------------------------------
    def classify(self, run_id: str, sha: str, base: Baselines, subset: list[str], ranked: list[str]) -> Verdict:
        """Wilson decision on D × k; INCONCLUSIVE → k more repetitions, then more tasks, up to the cap.

        If the cap is reached and it is still inconclusive, the point estimate decides and the
        step is flagged `low_confidence`.
        """
        first = self.evaluate(run_id, "bisect", sha, subset, range(self.cfg.k))
        if first.skipped:
            return Verdict.SKIP
        runs, kind = list(first.runs), "bisect"
        k = self.cfg.k
        # Only tasks that dropped from good to bad carry signal; a task that passes on both ends
        # adds cost and pulls the threshold towards 1. With none left, resample the subset again.
        widened = [t for t in ranked if t not in subset and base.drop(t) > 0][: self.cfg.discriminating_size]
        plans = [(subset, range(k, 2 * k)), (widened, range(k)) if widened else (subset, range(2 * k, 3 * k))]
        for round_ in range(self.cfg.max_resample_rounds + 1):
            threshold = base.threshold(runs)
            passes = sum(r.passed for r in runs)
            decision, low, high = decide(passes, len(runs), threshold, self.cfg.z)
            capped = round_ == self.cfg.max_resample_rounds or round_ >= len(plans) or not plans[round_][0]
            final = decision is not Decision.INCONCLUSIVE or capped
            with tracing.span("decision_rule", "TOOL", commit_sha=sha, input={
                "passes": passes, "n": len(runs), "threshold": threshold, "z": self.cfg.z, "round": round_,
            }) as sp:
                if decision is Decision.INCONCLUSIVE and capped:
                    verdict, flag = (Verdict.GOOD if passes / len(runs) >= threshold else Verdict.BAD), "low_confidence"
                elif decision is Decision.INCONCLUSIVE:
                    verdict, flag = None, None
                else:
                    verdict, flag = Verdict(decision.value), None
                sp.output({"decision": decision, "wilson": [low, high], "verdict": verdict, "flag": flag})
            step = self.ledger.get_step(run_id, kind, sha)
            self.ledger.set_decision(step["step_id"], verdict or Decision.INCONCLUSIVE, flag, low, high,
                                     len(runs), passes)
            self.log(f"  {sha[:10]} {gitops.subject(self.repo, sha)[:44]!r}: {passes}/{len(runs)} "
                     f"CI [{low:.2f}, {high:.2f}] vs t={threshold:.2f} → {decision}"
                     + (f" → {verdict} ({flag})" if flag else ""))
            if final:
                return verdict  # type: ignore[return-value]
            tasks, reps = plans[round_]
            kind = f"resample:{round_ + 1}"
            self.log(f"    resample {round_ + 1}: {len(tasks)} tasks × reps {reps.start}..{reps.stop - 1}")
            extra = self.evaluate(run_id, kind, sha, tasks, reps)
            if extra.skipped:  # cannot happen after a successful install, but stay safe
                return Verdict.SKIP
            runs += extra.runs
        raise AssertionError("unreachable")

    # whole run -----------------------------------------------------------------
    def start(self) -> str:
        return self.ledger.create_run(str(self.repo), self.cfg.good_ref, self.cfg.bad_ref,
                                      suite_hash(list(self.cfg.task_ids)), self.cfg.to_json())

    def run(self, run_id: str) -> Outcome:
        bad_sha = self.ledger.get_run(run_id)["bad_sha"] or gitops.resolve(self.repo, self.cfg.bad_ref)
        with tracing.run_context(run_id=run_id), tracing.span(
            "culprit_run", "WORKFLOW", commit_sha=bad_sha,
            input={"good": self.cfg.good_ref, "bad": self.cfg.bad_ref, "k": self.cfg.k},
        ) as sp:
            trace_id = tracing.current_trace_id()
            if trace_id:
                previous = self.ledger.get_artifact(run_id, "neatlogs_traces")
                self.ledger.put_artifact(run_id, "neatlogs_traces", f"{previous}\n{trace_id}" if previous else trace_id)
                self.log(f"neatlogs trace {trace_id}")
            try:
                outcome = self._run(run_id)
            except Exception as exc:
                self.ledger.finish_run(run_id, "error", None, None, f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
                raise
            sp.output({"status": outcome.status, "summary": outcome.summary})
            return outcome

    def _pin_suite(self, run_id: str) -> suite.PinnedSuite:
        """First run: snapshot the suite and record it. Resume: rebuild the recorded snapshot."""
        row = self.ledger.get_run(run_id)
        with tracing.span("pin_suite", "TOOL", input={"suite": self.cfg.suite, "suite_ref": self.cfg.suite_ref,
                                                      "recorded": row["suite_sha"]}) as sp:
            if row["suite_sha"]:
                pinned = suite.restore(self.repo, row["suite_source"], row["suite_sha"])
            else:
                pinned = suite.pin(self.repo, self.cfg.suite, self.cfg.suite_ref)
                self.ledger.set_suite(run_id, pinned.source, pinned.sha)
            sp.output({"source": pinned.source, "sha": pinned.sha})
        self.log(f"  suite pinned: {pinned.source} @ {pinned.sha[:12]}")
        return pinned

    def _ensure_tasks(self, run_id: str, good: str) -> list[str]:
        if not self.cfg.task_ids:
            assert self.pinned is not None
            with tracing.span("discover_tasks", "TOOL", commit_sha=good, input={"suite": self.cfg.suite}) as sp:
                tasks = discover_tasks(self.pinned.path)
                sp.output({"tasks": tasks})
            self.cfg = replace(self.cfg, task_ids=tuple(tasks))
            self.ledger.update_config(run_id, suite_hash(tasks), self.cfg.to_json())
        return list(self.cfg.task_ids)

    def _run(self, run_id: str) -> Outcome:
        cfg, repo = self.cfg, self.repo
        with tracing.span("git_rev_list", "TOOL", input={"good": cfg.good_ref, "bad": cfg.bad_ref}) as sp:
            good, bad = self._range(run_id)
            candidates = gitops.first_parent_range(repo, good, bad)
            sp.output({"good": good, "bad": bad, "candidates": candidates})
        if self.victim is not None:
            try:
                self.victim.require_key()  # e.g. a run started with Anthropic, resumed without the key
            except ProviderError as exc:
                return self._finish(run_id, "infra_error", None, f"Stopped: {exc}")
            self.log(f"  victim model: {self.victim.model} via {self.victim.name}")
        if not candidates:  # before the baselines, which are the most expensive part of a run
            return self._finish(run_id, "error", None, f"empty range: {cfg.good_ref}..{cfg.bad_ref} has no commits")
        tested: list[tuple[str, Verdict]] = []
        try:
            return self._bisect(run_id, good, bad, candidates, tested)
        except BudgetExceeded as exc:
            return self._budget_stop(run_id, exc, candidates, tested)
        except InfraError as exc:
            return self._finish(run_id, "infra_error", None,
                                f"Stopped: {exc}. Nothing was counted against the commit. Fix the cause, then "
                                f"`culprit resume {run_id}` continues where it stopped.")

    def _range(self, run_id: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        """Good and bad SHAs, resolved once; resume keeps them even if the refs have moved since."""
        row = self.ledger.get_run(run_id)
        if row["good_sha"] and row["bad_sha"]:
            return row["good_sha"], row["bad_sha"]
        good, bad = gitops.resolve(self.repo, self.cfg.good_ref), gitops.resolve(self.repo, self.cfg.bad_ref)
        self.ledger.set_range(run_id, good, bad)
        return good, bad

    def _bisect(self, run_id: str, good: str, bad: str, candidates: list[str],
                tested: list[tuple[str, Verdict]]) -> Outcome:
        cfg, repo = self.cfg, self.repo
        self.pinned = self._pin_suite(run_id)
        tasks = self._ensure_tasks(run_id, good)
        self.log(f"run {run_id}: {len(candidates)} commits in {cfg.good_ref}..{cfg.bad_ref}, "
                 f"{len(tasks)} tasks × {cfg.k}")

        base = Baselines(self.evaluate(run_id, "baseline", good, tasks, range(cfg.k)),
                         self.evaluate(run_id, "baseline", bad, tasks, range(cfg.k)))
        if base.good.skipped or base.bad.skipped:
            return self._finish(run_id, "error", None, "good or bad ref failed to install; cannot bisect")
        ci_good = wilson(base.good.passes, base.good.n, cfg.z)
        ci_bad = wilson(base.bad.passes, base.bad.n, cfg.z)
        self.log(f"  good {base.good.passes}/{base.good.n} CI [{ci_good[0]:.2f}, {ci_good[1]:.2f}]  "
                 f"bad {base.bad.passes}/{base.bad.n} CI [{ci_bad[0]:.2f}, {ci_bad[1]:.2f}]")
        p_value = fisher_one_sided(base.good.passes, base.good.n, base.bad.passes, base.bad.n)
        with tracing.span("regression_gate", "TOOL", input={
            "good": [base.good.passes, base.good.n], "bad": [base.bad.passes, base.bad.n], "alpha": cfg.gate_alpha,
        }) as sp:
            significant = base.good.rate > base.bad.rate and p_value < cfg.gate_alpha
            sp.output({"p_value": p_value, "significant": significant})
        self.log(f"  regression gate: one-sided Fisher p={p_value:.4f} (alpha {cfg.gate_alpha})")
        if not significant:
            return self._finish(run_id, "no_regression", None,
                                f"No significant regression to bisect: good {base.good.passes}/{base.good.n} vs "
                                f"bad {base.bad.passes}/{base.bad.n}, one-sided Fisher p={p_value:.4f} "
                                f"≥ {cfg.gate_alpha}")
        with tracing.span("select_discriminating_tasks", "TOOL", input={"size": cfg.discriminating_size}) as sp:
            ranked = self.ranked_tasks(base)
            subset = [t for t in ranked if base.drop(t) > 0]
            subset = subset[: cfg.discriminating_size] or ranked[: cfg.discriminating_size]
            sp.output({"tasks": subset, "ranked": ranked})
        self.log(f"  discriminating tasks: {', '.join(subset)}")

        result = bisect(candidates, lambda sha: self.classify(run_id, sha, base, subset, ranked), tested)
        low_conf = [s["commit_sha"][:10] for s in self.ledger.steps(run_id) if s["flags"] == "low_confidence"]
        confidence = "95% Wilson" if not low_conf else f"low: point estimate decided {', '.join(low_conf)}"
        if result.first_bad is None:
            summary = f"Culprit is one of {len(result.suspects)} commits (skipped commits hide the boundary): " + \
                ", ".join(s[:10] for s in result.suspects)
            return self._finish(run_id, "ambiguous", result, summary, confidence)

        with tracing.span("entire_checkpoint_explain", "TOOL", commit_sha=result.first_bad,
                          input={"sha": result.first_bad}) as sp:
            intent = commit_intent(repo, result.first_bad)
            sp.output({"available": intent.available, "checkpoint_id": intent.checkpoint_id,
                       "source": intent.source, "lines_removed": intent.lines_removed})
        self.ledger.put_artifact(run_id, "intent", intent.text)
        self.ledger.put_artifact(run_id, "diff", gitops.diff(repo, result.first_bad))
        self.log(f"  intent source: {intent.source}; leakage filter removed {intent.lines_removed} lines")
        summary = f"Culprit: {result.first_bad} {gitops.subject(repo, result.first_bad)!r} (confidence: {confidence})"
        return self._finish(run_id, "found", result, summary, confidence)

    def ranked_tasks(self, base: Baselines) -> list[str]:
        """Tasks ranked by pass-rate drop from good to bad (deterministic part of the Task Selector)."""
        g, b = base.good.task_rates(), base.bad.task_rates()
        return [t for _, t in sorted(((g[t] - b.get(t, 0.0), t) for t in g), key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1]))]

    def _budget_stop(self, run_id: str, exc: BudgetExceeded, candidates: list[str],
                     tested: list[tuple[str, Verdict]]) -> Outcome:
        lo, hi = bounds(candidates, tested)
        suspects = candidates[lo + 1 : hi + 1]
        summary = (f"Stopped: {exc}. Best current range: {len(suspects)} commits "
                   f"{suspects[0][:10]}..{suspects[-1][:10]}; tested {len(tested)} so far. "
                   f"Resume with `culprit resume {run_id} --budget-usd <higher>` to continue.")
        result = BisectResult(first_bad=None, suspects=suspects, tested=tested)
        return self._finish(run_id, "budget_exceeded", result, summary)

    def _finish(self, run_id: str, status: str, result: BisectResult | None, summary: str,
                confidence: str | None = None) -> Outcome:
        self.ledger.finish_run(run_id, status, result.first_bad if result else None, confidence, summary)
        self.log(summary)
        return Outcome(run_id, status, result, summary)

"""SQLite run ledger (PRD §12).

Every write is idempotent: steps are unique per (run_id, kind, commit_sha) and task runs per
(step_id, task_id, repetition). Resume works by replaying the deterministic controller, which
reuses any recorded step or task run instead of executing it again.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sqlite3
import uuid
from collections.abc import Iterator
from contextlib import contextmanager
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS runs (
    run_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    repo TEXT NOT NULL,
    good_ref TEXT NOT NULL,
    bad_ref TEXT NOT NULL,
    suite_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    suite_source TEXT,
    suite_sha TEXT,
    good_sha TEXT,
    bad_sha TEXT,
    config_json TEXT NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL,
    started_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    finished_at TEXT,
    total_cost_usd REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    culprit_sha TEXT,
    confidence TEXT,
    summary TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS steps (
    step_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    run_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(run_id),
    kind TEXT NOT NULL,
    commit_sha TEXT NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL,
    decision TEXT,
    wilson_low REAL,
    wilson_high REAL,
    n INTEGER,
    passes INTEGER,
    cost_usd REAL,
    latency_ms_p50 REAL,
    started_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    finished_at TEXT,
    error TEXT,
    flags TEXT,
    UNIQUE (run_id, kind, commit_sha)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS task_runs (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    step_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES steps(step_id),
    task_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    repetition INTEGER NOT NULL,
    passed INTEGER NOT NULL,
    cost_usd REAL,
    latency_ms REAL,
    tokens_in INTEGER,
    tokens_out INTEGER,
    neatlogs_trace_id TEXT,
    error TEXT,
    UNIQUE (step_id, task_id, repetition)
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS llm_calls (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    run_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(run_id),
    step_id INTEGER,
    purpose TEXT NOT NULL,
    model TEXT NOT NULL,
    tokens_in INTEGER,
    tokens_out INTEGER,
    cost_usd REAL,
    neatlogs_trace_id TEXT
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS artifacts (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    run_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(run_id),
    kind TEXT NOT NULL,
    path_or_text TEXT NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE (run_id, kind)
);
"""


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaskRun:
    task_id: str
    repetition: int
    passed: bool
    cost_usd: float | None
    latency_ms: float | None
    tokens_in: int | None
    tokens_out: int | None
    trace_id: str | None
    error: str | None = None


class Ledger:
    def __init__(self, path: Path):
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(path, isolation_level=None)
        self.conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        self.conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
        self.conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
        columns = {r["name"] for r in self.conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(steps)")}
        if "flags" not in columns:  # ledgers created before M2
            self.conn.execute("ALTER TABLE steps ADD COLUMN flags TEXT")
        run_columns = {r["name"] for r in self.conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(runs)")}
        # ledgers created before the suite was pinned, or before refs were resolved once per run
        for column in ("suite_source", "suite_sha", "good_sha", "bad_sha"):
            if column not in run_columns:
                self.conn.execute(f"ALTER TABLE runs ADD COLUMN {column} TEXT")

    @contextmanager
    def _tx(self) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
        self.conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        try:
            yield self.conn
        except BaseException:
            self.conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
            raise
        self.conn.execute("COMMIT")

    # runs -----------------------------------------------------------------
    def create_run(self, repo: str, good: str, bad: str, suite_hash: str, config_json: str) -> str:
        run_id = uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
        with self._tx() as c:
            c.execute(
                "INSERT INTO runs (run_id, repo, good_ref, bad_ref, suite_hash, config_json, status, started_at)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'running', ?)",
                (run_id, repo, good, bad, suite_hash, config_json, _now()),
            )
        return run_id

    def get_run(self, run_id: str) -> sqlite3.Row:
        row = self.conn.execute("SELECT * FROM runs WHERE run_id = ?", (run_id,)).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise KeyError(f"unknown run_id {run_id}")
        return row

    def update_config(self, run_id: str, suite_hash: str, config_json: str) -> None:
        with self._tx() as c:
            c.execute("UPDATE runs SET suite_hash = ?, config_json = ? WHERE run_id = ?",
                      (suite_hash, config_json, run_id))

    def set_suite(self, run_id: str, source: str, sha: str) -> None:
        with self._tx() as c:
            c.execute("UPDATE runs SET suite_source = ?, suite_sha = ? WHERE run_id = ?", (source, sha, run_id))

    def set_range(self, run_id: str, good_sha: str, bad_sha: str) -> None:
        with self._tx() as c:
            c.execute("UPDATE runs SET good_sha = ?, bad_sha = ? WHERE run_id = ?", (good_sha, bad_sha, run_id))

    def finish_run(
        self, run_id: str, status: str, culprit_sha: str | None, confidence: str | None, summary: str
    ) -> None:
        with self._tx() as c:
            c.execute(
                "UPDATE runs SET status = ?, finished_at = ?, culprit_sha = ?, confidence = ?, summary = ?,"
                " total_cost_usd = ? WHERE run_id = ?",
                (status, _now(), culprit_sha, confidence, summary, self.run_cost(run_id), run_id),
            )

    def run_cost(self, run_id: str) -> float:
        victim = self.conn.execute(
            "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(t.cost_usd), 0) FROM task_runs t JOIN steps s USING (step_id) WHERE s.run_id = ?",
            (run_id,),
        ).fetchone()[0]
        llm = self.conn.execute(
            "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cost_usd), 0) FROM llm_calls WHERE run_id = ?", (run_id,)
        ).fetchone()[0]
        return float(victim) + float(llm)

    def total_cost(self) -> float:
        """Cost across every run in this ledger, for the global (event-wide) cap."""
        victim = self.conn.execute("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cost_usd), 0) FROM task_runs").fetchone()[0]
        llm = self.conn.execute("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cost_usd), 0) FROM llm_calls").fetchone()[0]
        return float(victim) + float(llm)

    # steps ----------------------------------------------------------------
    def get_step(self, run_id: str, kind: str, commit_sha: str) -> sqlite3.Row | None:
        return self.conn.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM steps WHERE run_id = ? AND kind = ? AND commit_sha = ?", (run_id, kind, commit_sha)
        ).fetchone()

    def open_step(self, run_id: str, kind: str, commit_sha: str) -> int:
        with self._tx() as c:
            c.execute(
                "INSERT INTO steps (run_id, kind, commit_sha, status, started_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, 'running', ?)"
                " ON CONFLICT (run_id, kind, commit_sha) DO NOTHING",
                (run_id, kind, commit_sha, _now()),
            )
        row = self.get_step(run_id, kind, commit_sha)
        assert row is not None
        return int(row["step_id"])

    def close_step(
        self,
        step_id: int,
        status: str,
        *,
        decision: str | None = None,
        wilson_low: float | None = None,
        wilson_high: float | None = None,
        n: int | None = None,
        passes: int | None = None,
        cost_usd: float | None = None,
        latency_ms_p50: float | None = None,
        error: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        with self._tx() as c:
            c.execute(
                "UPDATE steps SET status = ?, decision = ?, wilson_low = ?, wilson_high = ?, n = ?, passes = ?,"
                " cost_usd = ?, latency_ms_p50 = ?, error = ?, finished_at = ? WHERE step_id = ?",
                (status, decision, wilson_low, wilson_high, n, passes, cost_usd, latency_ms_p50, error, _now(), step_id),
            )

    def set_decision(
        self, step_id: int, decision: str, flags: str | None, wilson_low: float, wilson_high: float,
        n: int, passes: int,
    ) -> None:
        """Decision over the commit's combined runs so far (initial step plus any resamples)."""
        with self._tx() as c:
            c.execute(
                "UPDATE steps SET decision = ?, flags = ?, wilson_low = ?, wilson_high = ?, n = ?, passes = ?"
                " WHERE step_id = ?",
                (decision, flags, wilson_low, wilson_high, n, passes, step_id),
            )

    def steps(self, run_id: str) -> list[sqlite3.Row]:
        return self.conn.execute("SELECT * FROM steps WHERE run_id = ? ORDER BY step_id", (run_id,)).fetchall()

    # task runs --------------------------------------------------------------
    def task_runs(self, step_id: int) -> dict[tuple[str, int], TaskRun]:
        rows = self.conn.execute("SELECT * FROM task_runs WHERE step_id = ?", (step_id,)).fetchall()
        return {
            (r["task_id"], r["repetition"]): TaskRun(
                r["task_id"], r["repetition"], bool(r["passed"]), r["cost_usd"], r["latency_ms"],
                r["tokens_in"], r["tokens_out"], r["neatlogs_trace_id"], r["error"],
            )
            for r in rows
        }

    def record_task_run(self, step_id: int, tr: TaskRun) -> None:
        with self._tx() as c:
            c.execute(
                "INSERT INTO task_runs (step_id, task_id, repetition, passed, cost_usd, latency_ms, tokens_in,"
                " tokens_out, neatlogs_trace_id, error) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)"
                " ON CONFLICT (step_id, task_id, repetition) DO NOTHING",
                (step_id, tr.task_id, tr.repetition, int(tr.passed), tr.cost_usd, tr.latency_ms,
                 tr.tokens_in, tr.tokens_out, tr.trace_id, tr.error),
            )

    # llm calls / artifacts ----------------------------------------------------
    def record_llm_call(
        self, run_id: str, step_id: int | None, purpose: str, model: str,
        tokens_in: int | None, tokens_out: int | None, cost_usd: float | None, trace_id: str | None,
    ) -> None:
        with self._tx() as c:
            c.execute(
                "INSERT INTO llm_calls (run_id, step_id, purpose, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd,"
                " neatlogs_trace_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (run_id, step_id, purpose, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd, trace_id),
            )

    def put_artifact(self, run_id: str, kind: str, text: str) -> None:
        with self._tx() as c:
            c.execute(
                "INSERT INTO artifacts (run_id, kind, path_or_text) VALUES (?, ?, ?)"
                " ON CONFLICT (run_id, kind) DO UPDATE SET path_or_text = excluded.path_or_text",
                (run_id, kind, text),
            )

    def get_artifact(self, run_id: str, kind: str) -> str | None:
        row = self.conn.execute(
            "SELECT path_or_text FROM artifacts WHERE run_id = ? AND kind = ?", (run_id, kind)
        ).fetchone()
        return None if row is None else str(row[0])
"""Read-only git queries against the victim repo. Nothing here touches its checkout."""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path


class GitError(RuntimeError):
    pass


def git(repo: Path, *args: str, check: bool = True) -> str:
    proc = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
        raise GitError(f"git {' '.join(args)} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()}")
    return proc.stdout


def resolve(repo: Path, ref: str) -> str:
    return git(repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{ref}^{{commit}}").strip()


def first_parent_range(repo: Path, good: str, bad: str) -> list[str]:
    """Commits after `good` up to and including `bad`, oldest first, first-parent only."""
    out = git(repo, "rev-list", "--first-parent", "--reverse", f"{good}..{bad}")
    return [line for line in out.splitlines() if line]


def subject(repo: Path, sha: str) -> str:
    return git(repo, "log", "-1", "--format=%s", sha).strip()


def message(repo: Path, sha: str) -> str:
    return git(repo, "log", "-1", "--format=%B", sha).strip()


def diff(repo: Path, sha: str) -> str:
    return git(repo, "show", "--format=", "--patch", "--no-color", sha)

from make_victim import build  # noqa: E402
